items.title: Section: Claiming Caste Supremacy, and the Three Faults That Disqualify Every False Claim

items.zh: 安立果者，謂彼種姓諸婆羅門，說阿素洛身應可殺害，天身是常；唯婆羅門最上種姓，餘姓下劣；廣說乃至諸婆羅門大梵所生，大梵所化，大梵支胤。彼種姓婆羅門作如是計，立如是論，當知是名安立果。如是種姓婆羅門，於此三處猛利取執，隨興言論：唯此是實是諦，餘並愚妄。何等名為由三過失染污其心？謂語言過失、憍慢過失、勝解過失。若即於此三處邪語業轉，當知是名語言過失。若復於此三處施設建立，及隨發起不正言論方比於他。謂己為勝、或等、或劣，當知是名憍慢過失。若復於此三處不觀德失，一向信受；雖遇諸佛及佛弟子正教誨時，於處非處不能正住，於遍分別不能正住，於諸正行不能正住，於智者論不能正住，當知是名勝解過失。此三過失，當知皆是惡見所起。若有住此三處，成就三種過失，雖是種姓諸婆羅門，依第一義，彼皆墮在非梵志數。
items.en: Regarding securing a result: these hereditary brahmins teach that asuras may rightly be killed while the gods' bodies remain eternally unchanging, and that brahmins alone constitute the highest caste, all others inferior. What are the three faults staining the mind? The fault of speech, the fault of arrogance, and the fault of misguided conviction. These three faults are all rooted in wrong view. Whoever dwells in these three places, bearing these three faults, however exalted their birth, is in the ultimate sense excluded from the ranks of genuine brahmins.

items.title: Section: The Genuine First Place — Harming No Being, Free of Speech, Arrogance, and Misguided Conviction Alike

items.zh: 復次，若有建立三處為諦為實，又於三處無三過失染污其心，彼雖非種姓婆羅門，然墮第一義婆羅門數。何等三處？謂不應害一切眾生，是名初處。此所說處，唯諦唯實，無有虛妄。是故於此初處，無語言過失染污其心。又彼於是處，不由諦實言論方比於他，謂己為勝、若等、若劣。是故彼於此處，無憍慢過失染污其心。又彼於此處審觀德失，觀彼所緣能增善法。又能攝益身心無罪現法樂住，於諸有情多住慈想，晝夜修學；又於此處非信他行，內自正覺為諦為實，然於諦實不妄執著。
items.en: Furthermore, whoever establishes these same three places as genuinely true, yet remains free of the three faults, though not born a brahmin, is in the ultimate sense counted among genuine brahmins. What are the three places? Not harming any living being is the first. This teaching is simply true and real, without falsehood, hence free of the fault of speech. In this, one does not, on the strength of its truth, compare oneself with others as superior, equal, or inferior, hence free of the fault of arrogance. It arises from direct, self-verified realisation rather than mere borrowed belief, hence free of the fault of misguided conviction.

items.zh: 是故當知，彼於此處，無勝解過失染污其心。

items.title: Section: Impermanence and Selflessness Complete the Three — And Only the Buddha Is the True, Complete Brahmin

items.zh: 如是一切行無常，是名第二處。餘如前說。一切法無我，是名第三處。餘如前說。此中差別者，於第二諦，應言於一切行多住生滅觀，晝夜修學。於第三諦，應言於一切法多住無我我所想，晝夜修學。若有於此三處無三過失染污其心，彼雖非種姓婆羅門，然墮第一義婆羅門數。如是三處成婆羅門諦實之法，離三過失。唯有如來是真覺者。
items.en: Thus impermanence pervading all conditioned phenomena is the second place, the rest as already explained. Selflessness pervading all phenomena is the third place, the rest as already explained. The distinction is this: for the second truth, one dwells largely in the contemplation of arising and ceasing, cultivated day and night; for the third truth, one dwells largely in the notion of no self and nothing belonging to self, cultivated day and night. Whoever holds these three places free of the three faults, though not born a brahmin, is in the ultimate sense counted among true brahmins. Though these three places constitute the very truth and reality of a genuine brahmin, free of the three faults, only the Tathāgata is the truly awakened one.

blocks.text: A short day. The treatise answers the brahmins' claims with three "truths" of its own: harm no being, all formations are impermanent, all phenomena are without self.
Claims of caste supremacy share the three faults: they are not true, they can be compared and challenged, and they are not personally realised.
Not harming any being: free of all three faults.

Not harming beings, the impermanence of all formations, and the selflessness of all phenomena: "these three places constitute the true doctrine of a brahmin". Master Cháng Bǎi: only the Buddha is the true, ultimate brahmin.
Mind and its factors, the afflictions, and the four truths. The fascicle ends by redefining a religious word: a "brahmin" is not born but made, by harmlessness and insight.

quiz.q: What are the three places of the ultimate brahmin, and how are they free of the three faults?
options: livelihood, merit, and result; done with a good mind they have no fault, and so they are the same as the hereditary brahmins' three
non-harming, impermanence of all formations, selflessness of all phenomena; true without falsehood, not used to compare, realised within and not by another's word
giving, discipline, and patience; free of fault when no return is sought
seeing, cultivation, and beyond learning, severing the three faults in turn
quiz.why: The treatise names not harming any being, the impermanence of all formations, and the selflessness of all phenomena. Each place is free of all three faults: true, no ground for comparison, and self-realised. Master Cháng Bǎi: after realising non-discriminating wisdom one awakens to not killing any being, not because someone said so. The English omits part of the passage on the third fault.

quiz.q: The fascicle closes with "only the Tathāgata is the truly awakened one." How does Master Cháng Bǎi conclude?
options: hereditary brahmins are the true ones and the Buddha merely borrows the name; the three truths come from the Vedas, not from him
all monastics are already ultimate brahmins
this says Brahmanism stands above the Dharma
only the Buddha is the true, ultimate, complete brahmin; the three truths of a true brahmin are established by the Buddha
quiz.why: The treatise closes that these three places constitute the true doctrine of a brahmin, free of the three faults, and only the Tathāgata is truly awakened to them. Master Cháng Bǎi: only the Buddha is the true, ultimate, complete brahmin, and the three truths of a true brahmin are established by the Buddha. So the title is reclaimed, not rejected.
